_comment: Virtual ad banners/billboards overlaid on top of convenience_store.glb (the GLB itself has no ad creative and, as of this file's last edit, no exterior geometry either - see StoreExterior.tsx for the procedurally-built parking lot + facade these outdoor billboards sit in). Positions are hand-placed in the store's world coordinates (see backend/data/store_layout.json store_bounds) to test the 'bonus' ask: does placement change how much attention an ad captures - now including *outdoor, open-space* placement, not just in-aisle. Edit freely - these are NOT derived from the GLB.
_ab_group_note: Every variant carries an ab_group ('a' or 'b'). One global variant_id selection (driven by the FIRST slot's variant_id, which also doubles as the session-level 'variant_id' field) resolves to the matching ab_group in every other slot too - so picking 'A' swaps the indoor endcap banner AND the outdoor billboard together as one coherent placement strategy, while each physical placement still keeps its own unique zone_id for independent attention tracking. See resolveAbGroup()/pickSlotVariant() in frontend/src/session/zoneLookup.ts.

ad_slots.description: Promotional banner - tests a high-traffic endcap placement (directly in the shopper's forward view from spawn, right above the cereal aisle) against a low-traffic back-corner placement.

Outdoor pylon billboard in the parking lot, facing the storefront entrance - tests the 'open space' ad placement bonus ask. Variant A is centered directly in the entrance sightline (high-traffic); variant B is off to the side near the lot's edge (low-traffic control), mirroring the same high/low-traffic contrast as the indoor endcap slot.

variants.label: Parking lot billboard - centered on entrance sightline (high-traffic)
Parking lot billboard - lot edge (low-traffic control)
